l-m-m2-b01-01.title: Is (a+b)² always equal to a²+b²?
l-m-m2-b01-01.goal: Check whether claim (a+b)² always equal a²+b² dey true, and find and explain one case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-m2-b01-01.material: Claim: for any two numbers a and b, (a+b)² equal a²+b². Find a and b wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-m2-b01-01.s.s1.r.a: (3+0)²=9 and 3²+0²=9, so dem equal. This example follow the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-01.s.s1.r.b: (0+5)²=25 and 0²+5²=25, so dem equal. This example follow the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-01.s.s1.r.d: Both values na 0, so dem equal. This example follow the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-01.s.s1.explain: (2+3)²=25 but 2²+3²=13. Since (a+b)²=a²+2ab+b², dem different whenever a×b no be 0.
l-m-m2-b01-01.s.s2.model.0: (2+3)²=25 but 2²+3²=13, so the two values different. Therefore a=2, b=3 na counterexample to the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-01.s.s2.model.1: If a=2 and b=3, the left side na 25 and right side na 13, so dem no equal. This show say the claim wrong.

l-m-m2-b01-33.goal: Check whether claim say other side always 5 cm dey true each time, then find and explain one case wey no (counterexample).
l-m-m2-b01-33.material: Claim: for right triangle with two sides 3 cm and 4 cm, the other side always 5 cm. Find case wey prove this claim wrong.
l-m-m2-b01-33.s.s1.r.a: Hypotenuse na the longest side, so 3 cm, shorter than 4 cm, no fit be am.
l-m-m2-b01-33.s.s1.o.b: When three sides na 3, 4, and 5 cm
l-m-m2-b01-33.s.s1.r.b: This example also follow the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-33.s.s1.o.c: When 3 cm and 4 cm form the right angle
l-m-m2-b01-33.s.s1.r.c: For this case hypotenuse na 5 cm, so example follow claim.

l-m-m2-b01-33.s.s2.model.0: If 4 cm na hypotenuse, 3²+x²=4² give x²=7, so other side na √7 cm. E no be 5 cm, so this counterexample.
l-m-m2-b01-33.s.s2.model.1: The longer of 3 and 4, wey be 4, fit also be hypotenuse, so other side no need be 5. That make claim wrong.

l-m-m2-b01-37.topic: Probability of event A or B
l-m-m2-b01-37.goal: Check whether the claim that probability of 'A or B' always be sum of the two probabilities always true. Find and explain a case where e no true (counterexample).
l-m-m2-b01-37.material: Claim: When you roll dice once, probability of event A or event B happening always na (probability of A)+(probability of B). Find two events wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s1.prompt: Choose the two events wey go against the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s1.r.a: 1/2+1/2=1, and the real probability too na 1. This example agree with the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s1.o.b: A: dice show 1, B: dice show 6
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s1.r.b: 1/6+1/6=1/3, and the real probability too na 1/3. This example agree with the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s1.r.d: 1/6+1/6=1/3, and the real probability too na 1/3. This example agree with the claim.
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s1.o.d: A: dice show 3, B: dice show 5
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s1.explain: Even numbers and multiples of 3 both include 6. Real probability na 4/6, but their sum na 3/6+2/6=5/6.
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s2.model.0: Even numbers {2, 4, 6} and multiples of 3 {3, 6} both get 6, so actual probability na 4/6. E no equal the sum, 5/6, so this na counterexample.
l-m-m2-b01-37.s.s2.model.1: 6 dey in both events, so when you add the counts, 6 count twice. That why sum 5/6 bigger than real 4/6.

l-m-m2-b01-19.s.s2.model.1: A solution must satisfy both equations at the same time, so check am like B. A only check first equation, so even wrong solution go pass.

l-m-m2-b01-23.s.s2.model.1: B longer at first, but e shrink 5 cm every minute and become short quickly, so starting length alone no tell which candle burn longer.

l-m-m2-b02-03.s.s2.model.1: Two x² together make 2x². Adding exponents na for multiplication only, so for addition you add the coefficients.

l-m-m2-b03-25.title: Wetin be equation after move graph 5 in y direction?
l-m-m2-b03-25.goal: Compare two ways or claims for shifting y=2x−3, choose better one, and explain why.
l-m-m2-b03-25.material: Graph of y=2x−3 move by 5 in y direction. A: y=2x−3+5=2x+2. B: y=2(x+5)−3=2x+7.
l-m-m2-b03-25.s.s1.r.a: You need add 5 to y to move am 5 in y direction. 2x+7 na equation wey shift up by 10.
l-m-m2-b03-25.s.s1.r.c: The y-intercepts for the two equations different, 2 and 7, so dem both no fit correct.
l-m-m2-b03-25.s.s1.r.d: A's equation correct because when you add 5 to y-intercept −3, you get 2.
l-m-m2-b03-25.s.s1.explain: Moving 5 in y direction add 5 to y-intercept. −3+5=2, so y=2x+2.
l-m-m2-b03-25.s.s2.model.0: Moving 5 in y direction add 5 to y value, so y=2x−3+5=2x+2. B's 2x+7 wrong because y-intercept increase by 10.
l-m-m2-b03-25.s.s2.model.1: Adding 5 to y-intercept −3 of y=2x−3 give 2, so y=2x+2. Slope remain 2, so A correct.

l-m-m2-b04-07.title: Which solving method simpler?
l-m-m2-b04-07.goal: For system 2x+3y=12, 2x−y=4, compare two methods or claims, choose best one, and explain why.
l-m-m2-b04-07.material: Solve system 2x+3y=12, 2x−y=4. A: Subtract one equation from the other to remove x. B: Rearrange one equation for y and put that into other.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.prompt: Which statement about the methods fit best?
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.o.a: B more accurate. Substitution always more reliable.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.r.a: Accuracy no different. Substitution just get awkward when fractions appear.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.o.b: A simpler. x coefficients same, so subtraction make x disappear.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.o.c: The two methods give different answers.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.r.c: If solve correctly, both methods give same answer.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.o.d: Adding both equations make x disappear.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.r.d: Adding give 4x, so x no disappear.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s1.explain: Subtract and get 4y=8, so y=2 and x=3. The coefficients same, so subtract simpler.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s2.model.0: Both x coefficients na 2, so subtract and x disappear straight away. Na why A simpler.
l-m-m2-b04-07.s.s2.model.1: Subtract and get 4y=8, so y=2 directly. Simpler than substitution, wey create fractions.

l-m-m2-b04-15.s.s1.o.a: A: If lengths ratio 2:3, areas also 2:3.
l-m-m2-b04-15.s.s1.r.a: Area grow in length and width, so multiply the changes.
l-m-m2-b04-15.s.s1.o.b: B: Area ratio na square of similarity ratio.

l-m-m2-b04-15.s.s1.explain: Lengths grow in two directions, so area ratio na 2²:3²=4:9.
l-m-m2-b04-15.s.s2.model.0: Area grow with both length and width, so square of similarity ratio 2:3, namely 4:9, correct.
l-m-m2-b04-15.s.s2.model.1: If one side become 1:1.5 times longer, area become 1.5×1.5 times, so B correct.

l-m-m2-b04-23.goal: Compare two methods or claims to check solution x≥4 of 2x−5≥3. Choose the better one and explain your thinking.
l-m-m2-b04-23.material: You solve 2x−5≥3 and get x≥4. A: Put only x=4 and check whether 3≥3 true. B: Put x=3 and x=5 too, together with x=4.

l-m-m2-b04-23.s.s1.o.a: A: Only put in boundary x=4

l-m-m2-b04-23.s.s1.r.b: A no catch wrong direction of inequality sign.
l-m-m2-b04-23.s.s1.o.c: B: Put in boundary and numbers on both sides
l-m-m2-b04-23.s.s1.r.d: Direction mistakes common, so checking necessary.

l-m-m2-b04-23.s.s2.model.0: x=3 must fail and x=5 must work for direction to be correct, so B, wey check both sides, more reliable.
l-m-m2-b04-23.s.s2.model.1: If you check only boundary, e pass even if answer wrongly be x≤4, so B, wey check both sides, better.

l-m-m2-b04-31.material: Find line through (1, 3) and (3, 7). A: Find slope first, (7−3)÷(3−1)=2, then put one point into y=2x+b. B: Put both points into y=ax+b and solve for a and b as a system.

l-m-m2-b05-34.topic: Count cases for sum on dice
l-m-m2-b05-34.goal: Compare methods for probability that two dice sum to 8, choose correct.
l-m-m2-b05-34.material: Find chance sum of two dice is 8. A: five outcomes (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2). B: order no matter. (8 5 2 6 3 5 4 4 5 3 6 2 5 36 3 2 6 3 5 4 4 3 36) (2.6 3.5 4.4)
l-m-m2-b05-34.s.s1.r.c: Answers differ, cannot both be correct.
l-m-m2-b05-34.s.s1.explain: Two distinguishable dice have 5 of 36 outcomes sum 8, so probability 5/36.
l-m-m2-b05-34.s.s2.model.0: Two dice distinct, (2,6) and (6,2) different, so 5 cases, probability 5/36.
l-m-m2-b05-34.s.s2.model.1: Only (4,4) happen once; other pairs have 2 orders, so 1+2+2=5 cases.

l-m-m2-b05-35.title: Is 7/48 a terminating decimal?
l-m-m2-b05-35.topic: How to know if decimal terminates
l-m-m2-b05-35.goal: Compare methods for determining whether 7/48 terminates; choose reliable one.
l-m-m2-b05-35.material: Find if 7/48 terminates. A: I divided several places and it didn't end. B: Look at prime factors of denominator. (7 48 48 2 3 3)
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s1.prompt: Compare methods and choose more reliable.
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s1.o.a: A: Dividing a few places enough.
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s1.r.a: Few places no prove whether e ends.
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s1.r.b: A only check part, no certainty.
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s1.o.c: B: Prime factors of denominator tell for sure.
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s1.r.d: Denominator 48 has prime factor 3, so decimal no terminate.
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s1.explain: 7/48 irreducible; denominator has 3, so decimal non-terminating. (7 48 3 0.14583)
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s2.model.0: Denominator in irreducible fraction 7/48 has prime 3; therefore know for sure it won't terminate.
l-m-m2-b05-35.s.s2.model.1: A few division places can't tell where it ends; B uses prime factors, so reliable.

l-m-m2-b0s5-08.title: Square fit be rectangle?
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.topic: How quadrilateral groups contain each other
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.goal: Compare two claims about whether square belong with rectangles, choose the better one, and explain your thinking.
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.material: Rectangle na quadrilateral wey all 4 angles be right angles. There be two views about square. (A) Square get all equal sides, so e no be rectangle. (B) Square get 4 right angles, so e be rectangle.
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s1.o.a: (A) The sides equal, so e no be rectangle
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s1.r.a: Rectangle meaning no include any rule about side lengths.
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s1.o.b: Rectangle suppose be longer than e wide
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s1.r.b: Rectangle meaning no get that condition.
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s1.o.c: Square na rhombus, so e no be rectangle
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s1.r.c: One shape fit be both rhombus and rectangle.
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s1.o.d: (B) E get 4 right angles, so e be rectangle
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s1.explain: Rectangle simply mean quadrilateral with 4 right angles. Square too meet this, so e be rectangle.
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s2.model.0: Rectangle only need 4 right angles, and no condition about side lengths. So square, wey all sides equal, also be rectangle.
l-m-m2-b0s5-08.s.s2.model.1: All 4 angles of square na right angles, so e fit the meaning of rectangle. (A) add condition wey no dey in the meaning.

l-m-m2-b01-20.title: Choosing suitable a in x+y=a
l-m-m2-b01-20.topic: Solutions of simultaneous equations and conditions
l-m-m2-b01-20.goal: Consider all conditions wey conflict when choosing a for simultaneous equations x+y=a, x−y=2. Choose the best compromise and explain why.
l-m-m2-b01-20.material: Choose a for simultaneous equations x+y=a, x−y=2. Both x and y must be natural numbers, and we want the smallest a wey keep the condition. The candidates na 2, 4, 5, and 6.
l-m-m2-b01-20.s.s1.prompt: Which a fit all the conditions?
l-m-m2-b01-20.s.s1.r.a: x=2 and y=0, so y no be natural number.
l-m-m2-b01-20.s.s1.r.c: x=3.5 and y=1.5 no be natural numbers.
l-m-m2-b01-20.s.s1.r.d: x=4 and y=2 natural numbers, but smaller a=4 dey.
l-m-m2-b01-20.s.s1.explain: x=(a+2)/2 and y=(a−2)/2. If a=4, x=3 and y=1, both natural numbers, and 4 na the smallest candidate wey work.
l-m-m2-b01-20.s.s2.model.0: If a=4, x=3 and y=1, both natural numbers. a=2 give y=0, and a=5 give x=3.5, so dem break the condition.
l-m-m2-b01-20.s.s2.model.1: The candidates wey give natural numbers na 4 and 6, and smaller better, so choose 4. When a=4, x=3 and y=1.

l-m-m2-b05-40.s.s1.explain: 2⁶=64 no enough, and 2⁷=128 reach 100. The smallest na 2⁷.
l-m-m2-b05-40.s.s2.model.0: 2⁶=64 below 100 and 2⁷=128 reach 100, so 2⁷ GB correct.
l-m-m2-b05-40.s.s2.model.1: 128 GB na the smallest capacity wey pass 100 GB among capacities wey double each time, so e be 2⁷ GB.

l-m-m2-b0s5-04.title: How many trips needed within elevator limit?
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.goal: Weigh all conditions wey clash for plan to move loads within a limit, choose the best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.material: Librarian wey weigh 65 kg dey move 22 book boxes, 12 kg each, using elevator. Librarian ride every trip, and elevator carry up to 200 kg for people and cargo together. You wan make as few trips as possible.
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.s.s1.prompt: Which plan stay within limit with fewest trips?
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.s.s1.r.a: 65+264=329 kg, wey pass the 200 kg limit.
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.s.s1.r.b: The trip with 12 boxes na 65+144=209 kg, wey pass the limit.
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.s.s1.r.c: E stay within limit, but 2 trips fit work, so this plan use too many.
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.s.s1.explain: 65+12×11=197 kg no pass 200, but 12 boxes go weigh 209 kg. 22 boxes fit move in 2 trips of 11.
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.s.s2.model.0: Up to 11 boxes for each trip weigh 197 kg, which work. 12 boxes weigh 209 kg, too much, so 2 trips of 11 be the fewest.
l-m-m2-b0s5-04.s.s2.model.1: To stay within limit, every trip must carry 11 or less. 22 fit move in 2 trips of 11, better than 3 trips.
